title: A combinatorial characterization of monadically NIP graph classes
formal: Resolved affirmatively: a class of finite graphs is monadically NIP if and only if it is flip-breakable. This supplies the purely combinatorial characterization requested in the 2023 source as an analogue of the flip-flatness characterization of monadic stability.
context:
Monadic NIP is defined through what a fixed logical formula can encode after arbitrary vertex coloring. The original request sought a purely combinatorial way to recognize the same class-level property.

In the 2023 theorem, a bounded number of flips can make one large selected set pairwise far apart. The requested NIP analogue was not a claim that this same stronger condition would suffice.

Flip-breakability requires two large sets to be far from each other after a bounded-part flip. Vertices within either set need not be far apart. This modified separation condition characterizes monadic dependence exactly.

The 2025 paper supplies another equivalent condition, weighted flip-separability. This strengthens the available structural descriptions without changing the fact that the historical characterization question was already answered in 2024.
why: Provides a graph-theoretic structural foundation for a logical class believed to organize the boundary of efficient first-order model checking.
status_note: Resolved by the published STOC 2024 characterization. The source question, theorem, graph-class scope and quantifiers were matched and the subsequent ICALP 2025 treatment checked. This is literature and model verification, not independent verification of the proof or a proof-assistant certificate.

A 2024 theorem provides exactly such a description, called flip-breakability.
After bounded-part adjacency flips, any sufficiently large vertex set contains two large subsets far from each other.
This condition is equivalent to monadic NIP for arbitrary finite graph classes.

references.title: Indiscernibles and Flatness in Monadically Stable and Monadically NIP Classes
references.authors: Dreier, Jan; Mählmann, Nikolas; Siebertz, Sebastian; Toruńczyk, Szymon
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 5; PDF page 5

definitions: A graph is finite, undirected and simple. A graph class C transduces all graphs if there is one first-order formula φ(x,y), using adjacency, equality and a fixed finite list of unary vertex predicates, with this property: every finite graph H can be obtained by choosing G∈C, assigning arbitrary subsets of V(G) to those predicates, joining distinct vertices u,v whenever φ(u,v) or φ(v,u) holds in that colored G, and taking an induced subgraph isomorphic to H. First-order quantifiers range over vertices; φ and its predicate list must be fixed independently of H, while G and its coloring may vary. C is monadically NIP, also called monadically dependent, if no such φ exists. A k-flip of G partitions V(G) into at most k parts and independently complements or retains adjacency between each unordered pair of parts, permitting a pair to consist of the same part; loops are never added. The resulting graph has the same vertices. C is flip-breakable if, for every integer radius r≥0, there exist an integer kᵣ and a function Nᵣ:ℕ₊→ℕ₊ such that for every m≥1, every G∈C and every W⊆V(G) with |W|≥Nᵣ(m), there exist A,B⊆W with |A|,|B|≥m and a kᵣ-flip H of G for which dist_H(A,B)>r. Here dist_H(A,B) is the minimum shortest-path distance between one vertex of A and one of B, with distance infinity across components. The constants depend on C and r, not on G,W or m. No hereditary-closure assumption is required for this equivalence.
answer_criterion: The affirmative answer is the published flip-breakability equivalence of Dreier, Mählmann and Toruńczyk, Theorem 1.3 in the full version. Its two directions exactly characterize all monadically NIP graph classes by a condition involving only graph partitions, adjacency changes, subsets and distances.
